trends.name: Iran War Escalation & Oil Shock
trends.summary: Trump administration escalating Iran conflict with stated intention to 'hit extremely hard' within weeks, while Iran rejects ceasefire talks despite US claims. Real-time X posts reveal IRGC now charging tolls through Strait of Hormuz in yuan/stablecoins, directly threatening global oil supply and inflation. Brent crude surged 5% as markets price in sustained energy disruption.

trends.name: Inflation Reacceleration & Cost Pressures
trends.summary: ISM prices paid index surged to 78.3 in March (highest since 2022), driven by steel/aluminum tariffs and Middle East oil shocks signaling entry into 'new inflation regime.' Real consumer spending contracting when adjusted for inflation despite headline retail sales beat, indicating stagflation risk. Supply chain safety stock building globally as manufacturers hedge war-related disruptions.

trends.name: Defense Sector Boom & War Beneficiaries
trends.summary: Geopolitical escalation driving defense spending surge across Europe and globally. Thales positioned for sustained growth amid elevated tensions. Defense contractors benefiting from multi-front conflicts (Iran, Ukraine, Israel-Gaza), creating structural tailwind for aerospace/defense equities.

trends.name: Electric Vehicles Demand Spike
trends.summary: BYD exports surged 65% in March as elevated oil prices from Iran conflict boost EV demand globally. Tesla delivery update imminent with analyst conviction in EV sector despite macro headwinds. Oil price shock creating structural tailwind for electrification adoption.

trends.name: SpaceX IPO & Mega-Cap IPO Wave
trends.summary: SpaceX reportedly making key strategic move signaling potential jumbo IPO, potentially catalyzing wave of large-cap IPOs. Market positioning for inflection in capital markets activity and growth stock valuations.

trends.name: Recession Odds Collapse & Fed Pivot Signal
trends.summary: Recession odds plummeted to 26% from March highs as markets price in soft-landing narrative and potential Fed rate cuts. April Fed meeting flagged as largest volatility event of month. Shift in macro expectations away from hard-landing scenario supports equity valuations.

trends.name: Amazon-Globalstar Acquisition Speculation
trends.summary: Globalstar stock surged 15% on reports Amazon weighing acquisition, signaling tech giant's push into satellite communications. Deal would strengthen Amazon's infrastructure moat and connectivity capabilities.

trends.name: Currency Debasement & Commodity Super-Cycle
trends.summary: US deficit at 6.2% of GDP (vs 40-year 3% average) driving currency debasement concerns. Multi-trillion capex needs ($2.5T data centers, $2T grid rebuild, robotics) requiring copper, aluminum, and steel create decade-long commodity super-cycle. IRGC toll payments in yuan/stablecoins signal de-dollarization.

trends.name: Consumer Spending Slowdown & Retail Weakness
trends.summary: February retail sales plunged with Q1 showing 'sneaky pullback' in real consumer spending when adjusted for inflation. Despite headline beats, actual purchasing power contracting signals consumer fatigue. Implications for consumer-facing equities and Q2 earnings guidance.

trends.name: Tech Layoffs & Oracle Workforce Cuts
trends.summary: Oracle fired 30,000 workers via email as tech sector continues efficiency purge. Broader trend of tech layoffs (Two Sigma leadership disputes, broader restructuring) raising questions about sector profitability and talent retention. Labor cost pressures easing but morale risks emerging.

trends.name: Nike Turnaround Failure & China Weakness
trends.summary: Wall Street losing patience with Nike as turnaround stalls and China market deteriorates. Apparel/consumer discretionary sector facing dual headwinds from macro softness and geopolitical trade tensions. Signals broader stress in consumer brands amid inflationary environment.

trends.name: Real Estate Debt Crisis & Brandywine Deterioration
trends.summary: Brandywine Realty Trust reveals hidden debt problems amid commercial real estate stress. Rising rates and office vacancy creating refinancing pressure for REIT sector. Structural headwinds from post-pandemic work patterns continue pressuring valuations.
